title: C: carbon nanotube sense-amp tier stacked above the array
idea: Print aligned semiconducting carbon nanotube films at <350 C on the bitline-contact level and build complementary CNT-FET latch sense amps and column muxes there, so the SA stripes move vertically over the mats instead of beside them. CNT's high mobility at 0.5-0.7 V keeps latch speed while the array below is untouched.
why: Periphery is ~49% of die (fact 7); lifting the SA stripes (~20% of die) above the mats could cut die area ~15-20% with a similar cost/bit gain and no litho node.

title: C: amorphous-carbon nanorelay row decoders with zero leakage
idea: Replace local decoder and sub-wordline-driver transistors with electrostatic diamond-like-carbon cantilever relays built in BEOL; carbon-on-carbon contacts resist stiction and wear, and a relay's infinite off-resistance and abrupt pull-in pass the full 3 V VPP with no gate-oxide stress.
why: Sub-wordline drivers are a large, leaky slice of periphery (fact 7, fact 10); stacked relays could halve decoder footprint and drop driver standby leakage to ~0; ns-scale nanorelay switching fits a ~30 ns row cycle.

title: Si: CCD bucket-brigade bitlines feeding one floating-diffusion amplifier
idea: Borrow the image-sensor trick: after a row opens, each cell's charge is clocked as a packet along a buried-channel silicon bitline to one ~1 fF floating-diffusion source follower plus comparator shared by 32-64 columns; restore is a reverse shift of a regenerated packet.
why: A ~1 fF sense node versus a ~60 fF bitline gives 10-50x more volts per electron, relaxing the Cs wall (fact 1) and cutting sense-amp count ~30x (fact 7); the cost is shift latency, suited to streaming or HBM-like page reads.

title: B: boron-doped avalanche junction as Geiger-mode bitline gain stage
idea: Place a tiny B/P-implanted p+n junction on each sense node, biased just below breakdown; the cell's few-thousand-electron surplus tips it into a self-sustaining avalanche (SPAD-style) that produces a rail-to-rail pulse, and an active quench transistor resets it in ~1 ns.
why: Gives digital-level output from a ~5 fF cell without a matched cross-coupled latch, potentially allowing Cs of 1-2 fF (fact 1) and smaller SAs (fact 7); risks are dark-count false triggers and breakdown drift with temperature.

title: Al+N: aluminum-nitride piezoelectric transformer generates wordline boost voltage
idea: Replace the multistage capacitive VPP charge pump with a Rosen-type AlN thin-film piezoelectric transformer driven at mechanical resonance from the 1.1 V rail; its 3-5x voltage gain plus a small rectifier gives the 3 V wordline supply without large flying capacitors.
why: Charge pumps occupy notable periphery area at ~30-40% efficiency; piezo step-up could cut pump area ~3x and raise efficiency toward 60%+, trimming the energy of the stuck 3 V wordline swing (fact 10).

title: Zn+Sn+Cu: indium-free oxide CMOS tier for row decoders
idea: Build n-type amorphous zinc-tin oxide and p-type Cu2O thin-film transistors in BEOL above the mats to host row decoders and wordline drivers; the wide-bandgap channels block 3 V with sub-fA leakage, and using only Zn, Sn, Cu and O avoids the indium and gallium of IGZO.
why: Moves decoder and driver area (a major part of fact 7's 49%) on top of the array using abundant elements; ~10-15% die area recovered and driver leakage cut ~100x.

title: Na: sodium-ion glass integrator counts each row's activations
idea: Attach to each row driver a tiny Na+-conducting glass cell encapsulated in SiN; every ACT pulse pushes a fixed quantum of Na+ across it, raising its conductance, and when a comparator crosses threshold the controller refreshes the neighbors and resets the cell with a reverse pulse.
why: Exact per-row counting today needs SRAM/CAM tables that balloon as the row-hammer threshold falls to ~1k (fact 9); an analog ionic counter under each driver costs ~no SRAM and gives deterministic protection.

title: Mg: MgO magnetic-junction coin-flippers drive randomized row-hammer refresh
idea: Use the thermally stochastic switching of low-barrier MgO tunnel junctions as a true random bit source in every bank, so each ACT triggers a neighbor refresh with tunable probability p, with no LFSRs, counters or tables.
why: Probabilistic row-hammer defenses need fast, unbiased, attack-proof randomness; one ~0.01 um2 MTJ per bank replaces counter tables, cutting row-hammer logic area >10x at ~1k thresholds (fact 9).

title: Ca: calcium-titanate varactor parametrically pumps bitline signal up
idea: Add a CaTiO3 paraelectric varactor to each bitline; after charge sharing, the sense-enable pulse biases it to drop its capacitance 3-4x, so the same signal charge appears as a 3-4x larger voltage before a smaller, less-matched latch fires.
why: Raises effective signal without more Cs (fact 1) and relaxes SA offset matching so SA transistors shrink, cutting SA area ~30-50% (fact 7).

title: S: sulfide threshold-switch matrix replaces per-wordline decoder transistors
idea: Place a two-terminal sulfide-based Ovonic threshold switch between each local wordline and two crossing global select lines; only the wordline at the driven intersection sees enough voltage to snap its switch on, so N wordlines need only ~2 sqrt(N) drivers.
why: Turns O(N) decoder/driver transistors into O(sqrt N) with BEOL two-terminal devices, roughly halving row-periphery area (fact 7); risks are half-select leakage and switch endurance at ~1e15 cycles.

title: Fe: iron-core inductors resonantly recycle bitline precharge energy
idea: Give each bank an on-die inductor with an electroplated Fe-Ni magnetic core; when sensing finishes, bitline charge is swung through LC resonance into the next bank's precharge instead of being dumped to the half-VDD rail, recovering roughly half of the CV2.
why: Attacks the voltage-floor CV2 energy (fact 10) of activate/precharge; claims 30-50% lower array activation energy.

title: Ti: titanium-oxide BEOL ROM stores per-row retention class
idea: At wafer test, measure every row's retention and write a 2-bit class into a TiOx resistive crosspoint ROM printed above the row decoder; the refresh counter reads the class inline and refreshes strong rows at 128-512 ms instead of 32-64 ms.
why: The leakage tail forces worst-case refresh (fact 3); multi-rate refresh cuts refresh operations ~70-80%, recovering 10-20% bandwidth and much of idle power with ~zero silicon area.

title: Zn: zinc-oxide thin-film varistors shrink I/O ESD clamps
idea: Replace bulky diode/SCR ESD clamps at each DQ and CA pad with a Bi/Mn-doped sol-gel ZnO varistor film in the pad stack, whose grain-boundary breakdown gives strongly nonlinear clamping and absorbs surge energy in volume, not die area.
why: Frees ~3-5% of die area in I/O periphery and lowers pad capacitance ~30%, which reduces I/O energy per bit (fact 5).

title: Sn: reflowable tin micro-links make field-reprogrammable repair fuses
idea: Replace one-time laser/e-fuses with Sn micro-links in sealed cavities: a Joule pulse melts a link so surface tension beads it open, and a second heater over wetting pads reflows it closed, so repair maps can be rewritten in the field as cells weaken.
why: Enables in-field repair of retention-weak rows (fact 3) and higher usable bits per wafer (~2-5%); reflow links pitch tighter than laser fuses.

title: Cu: hybrid-bond periphery wafers from idle U.S. mature-node fabs
idea: Split each DRAM into an array-only wafer from the DRAM fab and a periphery wafer (decoders, I/O, control, SA back-ends) made on 28-65 nm logic lines in U.S. fabs, joined by Cu-Cu hybrid bonding at ~1 um pitch.
why: Frees ~40% of expensive DRAM-fab wafer area per die for cells (facts 4, 7) and puts underused U.S. capacity to work (U.S. manufacturability); periphery gets faster logic transistors.

title: F: fluoropolymer ferroelectric caps hold trimmed reference per mat
idea: Use P(VDF-TrFE) (C, H, F) ferroelectric capacitors as partially polarized analog memories that set each mat's open-bitline reference level; at test the reference is trimmed to that mat's measured signal midpoint and held without DACs or fuses.
why: Mat-to-mat Cs and leakage variation erodes sense margin; centered references recover ~20-30 mV, buying longer refresh or smaller Cs (facts 1, 3).

title: Hf: hafnium-zirconia negative-capacitance gate boosts sense-amp gain
idea: Insert a thin HZO ferroelectric in the gate stack of the SA pull-down pair, matched for stabilized negative capacitance so the internal gate swing exceeds the bitline swing (~1.5-2x step-up) during sensing.
why: Pre-amplifies the ~100 mV signal, letting VARY drop below 1 V (fact 10) and SA transistors shrink; claims ~30% lower sensing energy.

title: V: vanadium dioxide insulator-metal switch as two-terminal comparator
idea: Bias a doped VO2 nanogap just below its insulator-metal threshold on each sense node; the cell's extra charge tips it metallic and hysteresis latches the result, replacing a 4-6 transistor latch with one two-terminal device. Doping shifts the 68 C transition above operating temperature.
why: SA area could fall ~3x (fact 7); the transition temperature and switching energy are open risks.

title: Al: anodic alumina nanopore forests as litho-free die-to-die vias
idea: Anodize an aluminum layer to self-order 20-40 nm pores, electroplate Cu into them, and use the vertical wire forest as a dense random interconnect between a stacked periphery die and the array; a calibration pass learns which pores join which pads.
why: Gives ~1e9-1e10 vertical connections per cm2 without EUV/ArF or tight bond alignment, enabling periphery-on-top stacking (fact 7) cheaper than TSVs (fact 6).

title: K: potassium-ion oxide electret supplies permanent negative wordline bias
idea: Drift K+ ions into a SiO2 plate under each mat's negative-wordline rail or back gate and lock them with a nitride cap, forming a stable electret (as in MEMS harvesters) that supplies a built-in -0.3 to -0.5 V bias with no VBB/VNWL charge pump.
why: Removes a pump and its standby current and area; a negative wordline low suppresses the leakage tail (fact 3), lengthening refresh intervals.

title: Ba: barium-titanate Pockels modulators replace DRAM DQ SerDes
idea: Bond epitaxial BaTiO3 electro-optic ring modulators at the DRAM periphery edge so each data group modulates light directly from the column data bus at 25-50 Gb/s, eliminating high-swing DQ drivers, termination and most SerDes logic.
why: DDR5 I/O at 10-20 pJ/bit (fact 5) could fall to ~1 pJ/bit and pad area shrinks; barium is abundant (barite).

title: Zr: antiferroelectric zirconia flying capacitors shrink charge pumps
idea: Build charge-pump flying capacitors from antiferroelectric ZrO2, whose field-induced phase change stores ~3-5x the energy density of linear high-k at 2-3 V, operated inside the double-hysteresis window to pump VPP and VBB.
why: Pump capacitors are among the largest periphery blocks (fact 7); 3-5x denser caps cut pump area accordingly.

title: N: liquid-nitrogen memory pods revive dies rejected for margin
idea: Sell 77 K immersion-cooled memory pods for data centers populated with DRAM dies that failed hot sense-margin or retention bins; at 77 K, MOS mismatch and leakage collapse, so these rejects run at full speed with almost no refresh.
why: Turns 5-15% scrap into product (more usable supply), cuts refresh power (fact 3) to near zero and widens SA margin; nitrogen is abundant, unlike helium.

title: Si: laser-crystallized silicon pre-amp per bitline segment, excimer-free
idea: Deposit a-Si (SiH4 in H2) over the bitlines and crystallize it with a diode-pumped solid-state 532 nm laser instead of a XeCl excimer (xenon plus neon fill) to form a source-follower pre-amp on every 32-cell bitline segment, which then drives a long global bitline.
why: Hierarchical gain lets 4x longer bitlines share each SA stripe, cutting SA count ~4x (fact 7) and decoupling the needed Cs from bitline length (fact 1).

title: Ti: titanium-oxo resist and 213 nm solid-state laser lithography
idea: Pattern periphery layers with a Ti-oxo-cluster photoresist exposed by a fifth-harmonic Nd:YAG 213 nm solid-state laser scanner instead of ArF/KrF excimers, whose gas fills are mostly neon plus argon or krypton; the Ti-O resist doubles as its own hardmask, dropping an argon-sputtered layer.
why: Removes the neon and krypton dependence from periphery patterning; periphery pitches of ~40-60 nm are reachable; ~20% fewer hardmask steps (fact 4).

title: Si: silicone block-copolymer self-assembly patterns regular decoder gratings
idea: Redesign decoders and sub-wordline drivers as strictly periodic gratings patterned by PS-b-PDMS directed self-assembly; the silicon-rich PDMS block becomes a SiOx hardmask in an O2/H2 plasma with no argon, and a coarse guide pattern from a non-excimer tool sets registration.
why: Replaces several neon-dependent ArF multipatterning exposures in periphery with ~10 nm self-assembly, cutting masks and capital (fact 4).

title: S: thiol monolayers self-align periphery contacts without lithography
idea: Use alkanethiol (C, H, S) self-assembled monolayers that bind only to exposed metal and block growth there, so dielectric grows only on dielectric in N2-purged area-selective ALD and vias self-align, removing via-litho layers and argon-sputtered liners.
why: Saves 2-3 masks per periphery stack (fact 4) and reduces contact-to-gate shorts so decoders pack tighter (fact 7), all without rare gases.

title: C: nanoporous carbon microsupercapacitors buffer activation current bursts
idea: Solution-cast nanoporous carbon electrodes with a gel electrolyte form a microsupercapacitor bank on the interposer or substrate under each DRAM stack, supplying the nC-scale ACT and refresh bursts so on-die decaps and VPP/VARY regulators can be ~3x smaller; processing is in air or N2, no argon sputter.
why: Decaps and regulators are a sizable part of periphery (fact 7); moving burst energy storage off-die frees area and steadies supply noise during sensing.

title: N: nitride charge-trap self-trim cancels sense-amp mismatch
idea: Give the SA cross-coupled pair an oxide-nitride-oxide gate stack (Si3N4 from SiH2Cl2 and NH3, N2 carrier); during test a feedback loop injects hot-carrier charge into the stronger device's nitride until the pair balances, permanently trimming offset.
why: Offset below ~5 mV allows ~2x smaller SA pairs and lower Cs (facts 1, 7), using only N, H, Cl and Si process gases.

title: Al: aluminum-polysilicon thermocouple mesh sets per-subarray refresh rates
idea: Lay Al / n+ poly-Si Seebeck junctions (Al by thermal evaporation, poly by LPCVD, no argon sputter) across the die; their uV/K outputs feed a shared chopper ADC so each subarray's refresh interval follows its own local temperature instead of the hottest spot.
why: Refresh is sized for worst-case temperature; hot-spot-aware refresh can cut refresh ops ~30-50% in cooler regions (fact 3) with near-zero-power sensors.

title: Zn: zinc-oxide acoustic resonator replaces the DLL clock
idea: Fabricate a ZnO film bulk acoustic resonator, with ZnO grown hydrothermally or by O2-only reactive sputtering rather than argon sputtering, on the periphery as a low-jitter GHz reference so the DQ path uses a small injection-locked oscillator instead of a large DLL.
why: DLLs and clock trees burn standby power and area; ~1-2% die area and ~10% I/O idle power saved (facts 5, 7).

title: Sn: tin-oxide Schottky diode matrices revive core-memory predecoding
idea: Spray-pyrolyze SnO2 films in air over the decoder region and form Schottky diode AND matrices, the 1950s diode-ROM decoding style, so row predecoding is done by stacked two-terminal devices and only final drivers stay in silicon.
why: Moves predecoder transistor area up and off the die plane (~5% die area, fact 7) with an air process and no critical lithography or rare gases.

title: Mg: water-dissolved magnesium sacrificial spacer creates air-gap bitlines
idea: Evaporate a thin Mg sacrificial spacer between bitlines, cap it with a porous lid, and dissolve it in dilute carbonated water to leave air gaps, avoiding the XeF2 (xenon) or argon-plasma release normally used for air gaps.
why: Bitline coupling falls ~40%, raising the transfer ratio Cs/(Cs+CB) (fact 1) so twice as many cells share an SA (fact 7) or Cs can drop.

title: Na: sodium-silicate water glass bonds periphery dies onto arrays
idea: Bond periphery dies face-to-face onto array wafers with a nanometer-thin sodium silicate adhesive cured at ~200 C, with Cu pillars electroplated through it and SiN barriers locking the Na; no argon/N2 plasma activation or argon-sputtered seed is needed.
why: Cheap, rare-gas-free die-to-wafer stacking moves periphery off the array die (fact 7) at lower capital than hybrid-bond tools and eases the TSV tax (fact 6).

title: H: deuterium-steam gate oxides quiet sense-amp telegraph noise
idea: Grow SA and decoder gate oxides in D2O steam and anneal in D2 so interface traps are capped by deuterium, which resists hot-carrier depassivation, lowering random telegraph noise and Vt drift that force SA oversizing; no rare gases are used.
why: Enables ~30% smaller SA transistors (fact 7) and steadier margin over life.

title: P: phosphorus-doped Esaki diode Goto pair as sense latch
idea: Use two degenerately doped silicon tunnel diodes (P and B gas-phase doping in H2, no argon-diluted implanter source) in series as a Goto pair on the bitline; the negative-resistance pair has two stable states and resolves a few-mV imbalance in tens of ps at ~0.3 V.
why: Breaks the ~1 V sensing floor (fact 10) and replaces a 4-6 transistor latch with two diodes; claims ~5x lower sensing energy.

title: Cu: electroplated copper coils link stacked dies without TSVs
idea: Replace HBM TSVs with inductive-coupling transceivers: spiral Cu coils, electroless-seeded and electroplated with no argon-sputtered barrier or seed, in each die's top metal pass data magnetically through 20-50 um of thinned silicon.
why: Eliminates TSV area, keep-out zones and TSV yield loss (fact 6, ~3x area per bit) at ~0.1-0.3 pJ/bit links.

title: Mo: molybdenum-chloride CVD replaces tungsten in periphery contacts
idea: Fill periphery contacts and wordline straps with Mo from MoO2Cl2 and H2 CVD (H2 carrier, N2 purge, no argon) instead of WF6 tungsten; Mo's short electron mean free path lowers resistance in narrow lines.
why: Lower resistance lets drivers shrink (fact 7) and removes the China-dominated tungsten chokepoint from periphery metallization.

title: Ni: nickel-silicide Schottky transistors make implant-free periphery logic
idea: Build periphery decoders from dopant-segregated NiSi Schottky-barrier MOSFETs formed by thermal silicidation, skipping ion implanters whose sources use argon dilution and purge; the abrupt metal junction shortens channels and limits short-channel leakage.
why: Removes ~10 implant masks and steps from periphery (capital, fact 4) and packs logic denser (fact 7) without rare gases.

title: O: electrochemically anodized gate oxides for room-temperature periphery transistors
idea: Anodize Zr or Al gate metal in an aqueous electrolyte so oxygen from water grows a self-limited ZrO2 or Al2O3 gate dielectric whose thickness is set by voltage (~1-2 nm/V), building BEOL periphery transistors without plasma ALD or argon sputtering.
why: Atomic-scale thickness control without vacuum tools enables cheap low-temperature periphery tiers over the array (facts 4, 7).

title: N: certified rare-gas-free periphery lines under CHIPS funding
idea: Create a federal certification and cost-share for N2/H2-only periphery lines: solid-state-laser or LED lithography, N2-purged ALD, H2-carrier CVD, electroplating, and H2 or N2 backside wafer cooling instead of helium; DRAM makers buying bonded periphery from such lines earn credits.
why: Insulates U.S. memory output from Qatar helium and neon supply shocks and seeds U.S. periphery capacity (U.S. manufacturability).

title: Si: silicon delay-line sensing tolerates variable rare-gas-free transistors
idea: Convert bitline voltage into delay by letting it bias the footer of a 16-stage current-starved Si inverter chain, then race it against a reference chain in a time-to-digital arbiter; averaging across 16 stages tolerates the larger device variation of periphery patterned with gas-free LED or solid-state-laser lithography.
why: Allows ~0.6 V sensing (fact 10) and relaxed periphery patterning; claims ~2x lower offset sensitivity than a single latch.

title: Fe: electroplated permalloy domain-wall counters track row activations
idea: Electroplate Ni-Fe nanowire loops (no argon PVD) as magnetic domain-wall counters, as in multi-turn rotation sensors, per row group; each ACT current pulse advances a wall one notch by spin-transfer, and an anisotropic-magnetoresistance stripe flags when a threshold notch is reached.
why: Nonvolatile, leak-free row-hammer counters (fact 9) without SRAM tables, ~0.1 um2 each in BEOL.

title: Ba: sol-gel barium titanate decoupling capacitors stacked over pads
idea: Spin-coat and cure sol-gel BaTiO3 (thin-film k ~200-500) MIM decoupling capacitors in top metal over pads and buses, processed in air or N2 with no argon sputtering, replacing the MOS decaps that fill periphery white space.
why: Decaps take several percent of die; moving them up frees ~3-5% area (fact 7).

title: Si: porous-silicon layer transfer reuses one seed wafer
idea: Grow periphery substrates as thin epitaxial Si (SiH2Cl2/H2) on an electrochemically porosified seed wafer (ELTRAN-style), split them off with a water jet and reuse the seed 10-20x, avoiding argon-purged Czochralski pulling and Spruce Pine quartz crucibles for most periphery wafers.
why: Cuts argon and high-purity quartz per periphery die ~90% and pairs naturally with bonded periphery; lowers wafer cost.

title: Ga+N: gallium-nitride UV-LED maskless lithography for relaxed periphery
idea: Expose non-critical periphery layers (>80 nm pitch) with dense arrays of 365/280 nm GaN/AlGaN micro-LEDs imaged through reduction optics, with no mask, mercury lamp or neon excimer, letting each die's periphery be customized (for example per-bin repair routing) at exposure.
why: Removes masks and neon-dependent tools from about half of periphery layers (fact 4) and enables per-wafer customization.
